proposals: SEBI should publish the findings of the fractional-share sandbox pilot and a dated decision on whether and how it will move beyond the sandbox, so that the one regulatory step towards direct fractional ownership of stocks like MRF is tracked to an outcome.

The Ministry of Corporate Affairs should issue a consultation paper on amending the Companies Act’s whole-unit shareholding requirement to allow fractional ownership, since that rule, not product design, is what keeps the roughly 530 stocks holding 60% of listed value out of reach of a ₹50 daily investor.

AMFI should publish monthly industry-wide data on daily-frequency SIPs — accounts, amounts and city tier, so that adoption claims such as 500,000 investors and 77% from tier-2 and tier-3 cities are visible across platforms and not only as figures self-reported by individual companies.
